task_text: Count the riders whose display name contains at least one letter outside the basic Latin alphabet A-Z (for example é, ø or ü). `result` should be that number (an integer).

Some trips have an empty duration_min. Fill each empty duration with the median duration of the other trips that started at the same station; if no trip from that station has a duration, leave it empty. `result` should be the full trips table with duration_min filled in.

Convert distance_km to whole metres, rounded to the nearest metre, and compute the total metres ridden by each rider. `result` should be a Series indexed by rider_id (with its leading zeros), sorted by rider_id.

Group the trips into distance bands: under 2 km, 2 to under 5 km, 5 to under 10 km, and 10 km or more. For each band, report the number of trips and the average fare (ignoring empty fares), rounded to 2 decimals. `result` should be a table with the columns band, n_trips and avg_fare, holding one line for each band.

Count how many riders joined in each calendar quarter, using joined_on and leaving out riders without a join date. `result` should be a table with the columns year, quarter (1 to 4) and n_riders, sorted by year and then quarter.

From the hourly weather, compute for each day the total rainfall and the highest temperature. `result` should be a table indexed by date, covering each day of September 2025, with the columns rain_total and temp_max.
Find the 5 riders with the greatest total distance ridden. `result` should be a table with the columns rider_id and total_km (rounded to 2 decimals), from the largest total to the smallest.

Look up the district of each trip's start station in stations.csv (tidy the district names: trim spaces and use title case) and count the trips that started in each district. `result` should be a Series indexed by district.

Make a table of trip counts with the payment method (trimmed, lower case) as rows and the rating (1 to 5) as columns, leaving out trips without a rating and using 0 where a combination has no trips. `result` should be that table.

Replace each rider's home district (trim spaces and use title case first) by the share of all riders who live in that district. `result` should be a table with the columns rider_id and district_share.
Trips that lasted longer than 60 minutes get a surcharge of 2.00 added to their fare; empty fares stay empty. `result` should be the full trips table with the updated fare column.

Summarise the trips by payment method (trim spaces and use lower case): the number of trips, the total fare, the mean distance_km and the share of trips that have a rating, all rounded to 2 decimals. `result` should be a table indexed by payment method with the columns n_trips, total_fare, mean_km and rated_share.

Each station name ends with a direction word. Split the name into base_name (everything before the last word) and side (the last word). `result` should be a table with the columns station_code, base_name and side.

Fill each empty temp_c with the average temperature of the same hour of the day over the whole month, rounded to 1 decimal. `result` should be a Series of all 720 hourly temperatures indexed by the observation time.

Convert credit_balance to whole cents (for example 4.97 becomes 497), counting an empty balance as 0 cents, and compute the total cents for each membership type, after trimming spaces and lower-casing the membership text. `result` should be a Series indexed by membership type.

Using age = 2025 minus birth_year, put riders into the age groups under 25, 25-39, 40-59 and 60 or older, and count the riders in each age group for each membership type (trimmed, lower case); leave out riders without a birth year. `result` should be a table with the age groups as rows and the membership types as columns.

Work out when each trip ended (started_at plus duration_min minutes) and count the trips that ended on a later calendar day than the one they started on; leave out trips without a duration. `result` should be that count.

Count the trips started on each calendar day and then take a 7-day rolling mean of these daily counts, treating days without trips as 0. `result` should be a Series indexed by day, from the first to the last day with trips.

For each payment method (trim spaces and use lower case), find the 3 longest trips by duration_min, preferring the smaller trip_id when durations are equal. `result` should be a table with the columns payment, trip_id and duration_min, sorted by payment and then from the longest to the shortest trip.

Join the trips to riders.csv by rider_id and compute the average fare per membership type (trim spaces and use lower case), ignoring empty fares and rounding to 2 decimals. `result` should be a Series indexed by membership type.

Make a table of the average temperature with the day of the month (1 to 30) as rows and the sky condition (trimmed, lower case) as columns, rounded to 1 decimal; leave a cell empty where that sky condition did not occur on that day. `result` should be that table.

Encode the payment method (trim spaces and use lower case) as an integer by how common it is: the most frequent method gets 0, the next 1, and so on. `result` should be a Series of these codes indexed by trip_id.

Set every negative credit_balance to 0 and add a column in_debt that is True for the riders whose balance was negative and False otherwise (including riders with an empty balance). `result` should be a table with the columns rider_id, credit_balance and in_debt.

Build a station flow report: for every station in stations.csv, the number of trips that started there, the number that ended there, and net_flow = ends minus starts (0 for stations without trips). `result` should be a table indexed by station_code with the columns starts, ends and net_flow, sorted by net_flow from highest to lowest.

Create a short code for each rider: the first three letters of the last name in capitals followed by the last four digits of rider_id (for example, Olga Rossi with id 004017 gets ROS4017); trim spaces in the name first. `result` should be a Series of codes indexed by rider_id.

For riders without a birth_year, use the most common birth year among riders of the same home district (trim spaces and use title case for the district); if several years are equally common, take the earliest. `result` should be a table with the columns rider_id, home_district and birth_year.
Turn the fare into display text with a euro sign and two decimals (for example €3.10), writing n/a for an empty fare. `result` should be a Series of these labels indexed by trip_id.

Classify each hour's wind_kmh as calm (0-5), breeze (6-20), windy (21-35) or strong (36 and above), and report for each class the number of hours and the total rain_mm (rounded to 1 decimal). `result` should be a table indexed by class with the columns hours and rain_total.
For each station, compute the year it opened and the number of days from its opening date to 2025-12-31. `result` should be a table with the columns station_code, opened_year and days_open.

Compute six-hour averages of temp_c and wind_kmh, in blocks starting at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 each day. `result` should be a table indexed by the start of each block with the columns temp_c and wind_kmh, rounded to 2 decimals.

List the 10 riders with the highest credit_balance, taking the smaller rider_id first when balances are equal. `result` should be a table with the columns rider_id, display_name (spaces trimmed) and credit_balance, from the highest balance down.

Using fare_changes.csv, count how many trips started at a station with a planned fare change, separately for each planned new_base_fare value; leave out stations whose planned fare is empty. `result` should be a Series indexed by new_base_fare.
